A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VQ-AE-based steering localization work, renamed from DEAL to REAL. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. V1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: V1 reports original truthfulness, general-behavior and cross-domain steering experiments, alongside representation analyses and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds knowledge-conflict evaluations, localization diagnostics and generated responses for all 817 TruthfulQA questions.

M1.justification: The core VQ-AE, contrastive loss, autoregressive prior and AUC-based scoring remain. V2 adds direct whole-layer scoring coupled with SPARE-style SAE interventions (Section 4.2). Appendix A also changes the reported encoder/decoder from two-layer 128/64 MLPs to one-layer dimension-halving maps. Noisy-OR layer aggregation already existed in v1.

E1.justification: V1 already uses TruthfulQA, MQuAKE, CLUTRR and four AI-risk datasets. V2 retains these and adds NQSwap and MacNoise for selecting contextual versus parametric answers under conflicting evidence, introducing a substantive new task scenario. Appendix D additionally reports free-form generations on the existing TruthfulQA questions.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained ITI, LoFiT and no-steering comparisons, v2 Table 2 adds CD, DoLa, TruthX, TruthFlow and AD for selected models. The new knowledge-conflict comparison includes TaskVec, ActAdd, two SEA variants, DoLa, CAD, ICL and SPARE (Table 4). These methods participate in reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The new knowledge-conflict experiments introduce Llama3-8B, three non-conflicting demonstrations per question, separate contextual/parametric exact-match evaluations and seven selected intervention layers. Appendix C specifies 30 VQ-AE and 10 GRU training epochs for this application. Existing head-selection budgets and general-behavior intervention protocols remain; newly disclosed existing splits do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The existing representation, head-heatmap, data-size and hyperparameter analyses are retained. V2 adds an ITI–REAL head-overlap comparison, three interpreted generation examples supported by Appendix D, and a zero-contrastive-loss control in Figure 6c. These are targeted extensions to the existing analysis suite.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three independent random runs. V2 first supplies ± values for REAL's TruthfulQA results and for the knowledge-conflict comparisons. The PDFs do not specify whether these denote standard deviations or another uncertainty statistic, and no increase in run count is established.

E6.justification: V2 adds knowledge-conflict scores, additional baseline results, layer rankings and generation outputs. Reported Qwen2.5-7B ITI MC1/MC2 change from 30.72/45.79 to 35.92/52.95; its proposed-method full-data ablation entry changes from 41.86 to 45.59 MC1. Most retained proposed-method TruthfulQA means, transfer accuracies and four-behavior probabilities remain unchanged. These revisions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Core Equations 1–6 and the training losses remain mathematically unchanged. Appendix B adds explicit definitions of average head confidence, the fraction above a global percentile threshold and their noisy-OR combination, including an independent-event interpretation. V1 only mentions this composite; neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central improved-steering and zero-shot-transfer claims, including the stated 20% average and 81.5% maximum improvement, remain. V2 extends the headline contribution to head/layer localization and knowledge-conflict control, drops the causal-attribution characterization, and adds qualitative claims about grounded specificity and calibrated refusal.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning truthfulness–informativeness trade-offs, calibrated abstention and conflicting knowledge sources. It states SAE-availability and storage limitations for knowledge-selection experiments and clarifies CAA's analytical role. It also removes v1's inference that data efficiency demonstrates structural regularities rather than memorization; the main disentanglement and GQA interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies dataset split counts, two-fold TruthfulQA evaluation, batch size 16, GPU capacity, per-head/per-layer training time and memory, and parallel training counts. Appendices B–C document previously underspecified aggregation and new layer-training hyperparameters. These substantially expand reproducibility information, while most existing head-training rates, epochs and software versions are retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around learned steering, dynamic intervention strength and SAE-based knowledge selection through TruthFlow, LITO and SPARE. It adds knowledge-conflict, misinformation, benchmark and comparator literature, while dropping CCS and several earlier citations. This changes research coverage beyond relocating the former related-work section.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming DEAL to REAL and editing the title/authorship, v2 substantially rewrites the introduction and preliminaries, organizes experiments by application, consolidates analyses, and integrates related work into the background. Implementation material moves to Appendix A, with additional appendices extending the structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds generation-example and head-overlap figures, several dataset/result/diagnostic tables, and boxed response listings. It transposes and expands the TruthfulQA table, reformats transfer results, and incorporates the former contrastive-loss table into Figure 6. Existing framework, representation and heatmap graphics are retained with relocation and caption changes.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical scrutiny through broader baselines and knowledge-conflict evaluation, while added implementation details and complete generated responses improve transparency. However, revised Qwen2.5-7B ITI scores retain stale relative gains in Table 2, and Table 6 contradicts the claimed smaller loss from halving REAL's training data. These reporting problems limit confidence in the expanded claims and constrain the overall improvement.
